clue.text: Part of hotel with no heating - it’s not very welcoming

blocks.note: a room with no heating is cold
the front desk area of a hotel

explanation.surface: A hotel lobby left unheated makes arriving guests feel unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are taken in reverse of their clue order: the unheated state comes first, then the hotel area.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold greeting is the idiom for an unfriendly response, so an unwelcoming manner fits exactly.

clue.text: Long to be in Connecticut - indication of superior status

indicators.note: one word is told to sit inside the other, so it is placed within

blocks.note: postal abbreviation of the US state
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearning to live in Connecticut as a mark of prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet means prestige or distinction, the mark that signals high social standing.

clue.text: One politician everyone's determined to arraign

explanation.surface: A lone politician whom the whole house is set on putting on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is a Member of Parliament, the usual crossword politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to bring formal charges against an official, which is what arraigning someone involves.

clue.text: Family party at first presenting management problem?

indicators.note: says the political party is placed at the front of the family word

explanation.surface: A family gathering that, early on, turns into a headache for whoever runs it.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of Britain's two big political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealings between employers and workforce are a classic area of difficulty for company bosses, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Jackets some people roll up?

blocks.note: first meaning: short thick double-breasted coats worn by sailors

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests people rolling up their sleeves; the second meaning is slang for a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a naval-style coat and, in slang, a rolled marijuana cigarette.

clue.text: Brigand off in a trance

indicators.note: something off is not right, so these letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An outlaw who has drifted off into a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: A cateran is a Highland raider, an old Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cateran was a marauding Scottish Highland irregular, a robber or bandit.

clue.text: Advantage in only getting a single ticket?

definitions.text: Advantage in only getting a single ticket?

blocks.note: a point is an advantage or merit, as in 'that's a point in its favour'
a single ticket is a one-way fare, with no return leg

explanation.surface: A traveller weighing up the perks of a one-way fare.
explanation.walkthrough: Advantage can mean a point, and a single ticket is one without a return leg; together they name the stage after which one is committed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for the moment past which going back becomes impossible, like a one-way trip.

clue.text: Lily's poor attitude, upset in old Adriatic place

indicators.note: a poor version is a badly made one, so the name is rearranged
in a down clue, upset means turned over, so the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: the name, worked by the anagram
an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: Lily's sulky mood turns sour while on holiday on the old Adriatic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Illyria was the ancient region on the eastern Adriatic shore, also the setting of Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyria was the classical name for the Balkan coastland along the Adriatic Sea.

clue.text: US noodle of unusual type, with small lumps

indicators.note: an unusual type is an irregular form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: An odd kind of American pasta that comes out lumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulose describes something bearing nodules, which are small knobs or swellings.

clue.text: Message secretary's brought in, showing competence

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, here the secretary goes inside the message

blocks.note: first part of a cable, a telegram

explanation.surface: An office scene where the secretary delivers a message and proves efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: A cable is a telegram; PA, a personal assistant, sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable describes having the ability to do things well, the adjective for showing competence.

clue.text: Made musical sounds, having worked to comprehend guitar, finally

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of the instrument named
to comprehend is to take in or include, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: first letter of tilled, worked as land is

explanation.surface: A musician warbled away while getting to grips with a guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: Worked here is farming: to till the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To trill is to sing or play with a rapid quavering alternation of notes.

clue.text: Time certain to lead to cancellation

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something is bound in time to end in cancellation.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a deletion or rubbing out, the act of wiping something away.

clue.text: Withdrawing censored trailer

indicators.note: censored material is cut about and altered, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A film trailer cut by the censor and pulled from cinemas.
explanation.walkthrough: Retiral is chiefly Scottish usage for retirement or withdrawal; the definition is a noun use of the -ing form.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiral is a Scottish word for retirement, the act of stepping back or pulling out.

clue.text: Not the sounds heard naturally?

blocks.note: surface reading: artificial noises, not those of nature
setter's reading: in music a natural is an unaltered note, so these are the notes raised or lowered from it

explanation.surface: A puzzle about sounds that are not natural, as opposed to birdsong.
explanation.walkthrough: In notation, a natural sign cancels a raise or lowering of a note; these are the raised and lowered notes themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical notes altered up or down a semitone are the opposite of naturals in notation.

clue.text: American doctor's about to go to dance in liquor store

indicators.note: about means around, so the doctor's word wraps the other piece

blocks.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: An American doctor heads to a dance being held in an off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor's possessive gives DRS, which goes around AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramshop is an old term for a bar or tavern selling spirits by the dram.

clue.text: ‘They have their exits and their entrances’

definitions.text: They have their exits and their entrances

blocks.clueFragment: They have their exits and their entrances
blocks.note: surface reading: Shakespeare's line about men and women as players on life's stage

blocks.clueFragment: They have their exits and their entrances
blocks.note: setter's reading: spinning doors that people constantly enter and leave by

explanation.surface: A quotation from As You Like It's 'All the world's a stage' speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks point to Jaques's speech, where players come and go; taken literally, the line describes rotating doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating entrance doors at hotels and offices serve as both the way out and the way in.

clue.text: Caustic solution - it initially ruined old instrument's exterior

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word that follows
the instrument is the exterior, so it forms the outside around the rest

blocks.note: first half of viol, an early stringed instrument

explanation.surface: An acid ate away the outside of an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: A viol is a Renaissance bowed instrument, ancestor of the violin family.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is the old name for sulphuric acid, a corrosive liquid.

clue.text: Student leaves stupid duelling to have a drink

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer present, so that letter is taken out
a stupid arrangement is a senseless one, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A student quits pointless sword fighting to go for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: One L is removed from the eight letters before they are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge, used informally, means to allow oneself alcohol, a common euphemism.

clue.text: Checked material required for staging Hamlet

indicators.note: the letters needed are drawn from within the following words

explanation.surface: A wardrobe department needs checked fabric for its Hamlet production.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a cotton fabric woven with a pattern of coloured squares.

clue.text: English farmer about to put painting in new surround

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: An English farmer is about to remount a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To reframe a picture is to mount it within a different border.

clue.text: Those who regularly work with tools?

blocks.note: first meaning: people who ply, that is, work steadily at a trade
second meaning: pincers used for gripping and bending wire

explanation.surface: Craftsmen who handle tools as part of their daily trade.
explanation.walkthrough: To ply is to work regularly at something, so those who ply are one meaning; the question mark flags that rarer sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pincer-like gripping instrument and, less commonly, people who ply a trade.

clue.text: Troops in quiet environment were transformed

indicators.note: the troops sit within the quiet setting described

explanation.surface: Soldiers stationed somewhere peaceful find themselves changed.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: To have mutated is to have changed form, a past-tense match for being transformed.

clue.text: What's necessary to end fuel crisis?

indicators.note: a crisis throws things into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking what must be done to resolve a fuel shortage.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun, 'the needful' is what is required, as in 'do the needful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The needful is an idiomatic noun for whatever is required, especially money or action.

clue.text: Film sometimes put on before parting?

definitions.text: Film sometimes put on before parting?

blocks.clueFragment: Film sometimes put on before parting?
blocks.note: surface reading: a movie shown before guests leave

blocks.clueFragment: Film sometimes put on before parting?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a thin coating applied before combing a line through the hair

explanation.surface: A film screened as a farewell before people go their separate ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Film is a thin layer, and a parting is the line combed in the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliantine and similar oils are smeared on the scalp before combing a neat parting.

clue.text: Transport provided by a huge conglomerate around US city

indicators.note: a conglomerate is a mixed mass, so the letters are mixed up
the jumbled letters go around the city

explanation.surface: A vast business group based in an American city runs the freight.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the business of carrying goods by road, a kind of freight transport.

clue.text: Shining examples of courteous behaviour?

blocks.note: something polished has been rubbed until it shines
acts of politeness are good manners

explanation.surface: Praise for people who set a fine example of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: Shining is taken literally, as something rubbed until it gleams, while the whole clue also reads as praise of refined conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined, elegant etiquette is described idiomatically as smooth and buffed, like a gleaming surface.
